I designed and launched a network of 436 programmatic route pages, then rebuilt the conversion journey, app store presence and tracking behind them.
Topship had a strong product and fair prices. But its website barely showed up in search.
Most new customers came through paid ads. In a crowded market, that’s an expensive way to grow.

Organic search went from a minor channel to the biggest source of new sign-ups. Over the same period, Topship kept breaking its monthly delivery record. Pages ranked on page one for searches like “shipping from Lagos to Abuja”, “delivery from Nigeria to UK”, and “express delivery Lagos”.
We started with search demand, not a content calendar. We listed every route Topship served, then checked how people searched for each.

Programmatic pages often fail because they’re thin. So we set rules every page had to meet before it went live.

On the homepage, we built two hero sections for different customer types. We added app reviews and social proof, plus app prompts below the hero and above the footer.

After sign-up, a 14-day onboarding flow taught new users how to ship. An abandoned shipment flow brought back people who started an order and stopped. Anyone inactive for 30 days or more got a reactivation campaign.
The order confirmation page, the welcome email, and every transactional email carried an app download prompt with social proof.

In the app stores, we optimised the title and description for terms like “shipping”, “delivery”, “logistics”, and “interstate delivery”. We improved the icon and screenshots, and asked for a review after each successful delivery. A dedicated landing page showed off the app’s features.
You can’t improve what you can’t see. So we rebuilt Topship’s tracking across web and app.
The apps got Firebase, their own GA4 property, the Facebook SDK, and OneSignal for push messages. Mixpanel and session recordings showed where users dropped off.

On Google Ads, we linked GA4 for conversions and audiences, ran app install campaigns, and excluded existing customers. On Meta, we made separate creative for new customers and for moving existing ones to the app. Retargeting followed site visitors and anyone who abandoned a shipment.
